420	@app.post("/orgs", status_code=201)
421	def create_org(
422	    body: CreateOrgRequest,
423	    request_body: bytes = Depends(raw_body),
424	    user: CurrentUser = Depends(current_user),
425	    conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_conn),
426	    idempotency_key: Optional[str] = Header(default=None, alias="Idempotency-Key", max_length=128),
427	    authorization: Optional[str] = Header(default=None),
428	    x_session_token: Optional[str] = Header(default=None, alias="X-Session-Token"),
429	) -> dict[str, Any]:
430	    # The one session actually carried by THIS request (Bearer or
431	    # X-Session-Token; ``_extract_token`` keeps the existing precedence).
432	    # ``user`` only proves it was valid when the request arrived; the
433	    # creation — and any idempotent replay — must be authorized by the
434	    # session state at the moment it runs inside the write transaction.
435	    request_token = _extract_token(authorization, x_session_token)
436	    if not request_token:  # defense in depth; current_user already 401s here
437	        raise unauthorized()
438	
439	    def _perform(c: sqlite3.Connection, ts: int) -> tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]:
440	        if c.execute("SELECT 1 FROM organizations WHERE name = ?", (body.name,)).fetchone():
441	            raise conflict("org_name_taken", "organization name is already taken")
442	        try:
443	            org_cur = c.execute(
444	                "INSERT INTO organizations (name, created_by, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
445	                (body.name, user.id, ts),
446	            )
447	        except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
448	            # Concurrent creation of an organization with the same name.
449	            raise conflict("org_name_taken", "organization name is already taken")
450	        org_id = org_cur.lastrowid
451	        c.execute(
452	            "INSERT INTO memberships (org_id, user_id, role, status, created_at, updated_at)"
453	            " VALUES (?, ?, 'admin', 'active', ?, ?)",
454	            (org_id, user.id, ts, ts),
455	        )
456	        add_audit(
457	            c, org_id=org_id, actor_id=user.id, action="org.created",
458	            target_type="organization", target_id=org_id,
459	            before=None, after={"id": org_id, "name": body.name}, ts=ts,
460	        )
461	        return 201, {"id": org_id, "name": body.name, "role": "admin", "created_at": ts}
462	
463	    def _check_session(c: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
464	        # Re-validate INSIDE the IMMEDIATE transaction, before the name check,
465	        # the idempotency lookup and any write. BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes us
466	        # against logout / logout-others / password-change writers: a session
467	        # revoked or expired while the request waited on the lock fails closed
468	        # with 401, leaving no organization, no admin membership, no audit and
469	        # no idempotency record. Another valid session of the account cannot
470	        # substitute — the check is keyed to this token alone. Runs on the
471	        # first attempt, the concurrent-key replay, and stored replays alike.
472	        revalidate_session(c, request_token, now_ts())
473	
474	    _, resp = _run_idempotent(
475	        conn, user, idempotency.scope_org_create(), idempotency_key, request_body,
476	        check_perm=_check_session, perform=_perform,
477	    )
478	    return resp

584	def _active_delegation(c: sqlite3.Connection, org_id: int, user_id: int, ts: int) -> sqlite3.Row:
585	    """Return the caller's currently active delegation or raise 403.
586	
587	    A delegation is active only while status is ``active`` AND the expiry
588	    instant has not arrived; from the expiry moment on it authorizes nothing.
589	    """
590	    d = c.execute(
591	        """
592	        SELECT * FROM delegations
593	        WHERE org_id = ? AND delegate_id = ? AND status = 'active'
594	        """,
595	        (org_id, user_id),
596	    ).fetchone()
597	    if d is None or d["expires_at"] <= ts:
598	        raise forbidden()
599	    return d
600	
601	
602	# Eligibility rules behind a delegation, in ONE place. A delegation stays
603	# effective only while its grantor is an ACTIVE administrator and its
604	# delegate is an ACTIVE ordinary member of the same organization. Both the
605	# lazy sweep below and the member-change invalidation after PATCH (single
606	# and batch entry points) derive their reasons from these predicates, so a
607	# new eligibility rule is defined here once. Role/status may be None when a
608	# membership row is missing (e.g. direct on-disk manipulation) — that never
609	# qualifies.
610	def _grantor_qualifies(role: Optional[str], status: Optional[str]) -> bool:
611	    return role == "admin" and status == "active"
612	
613	
614	def _delegate_qualifies(role: Optional[str], status: Optional[str]) -> bool:
615	    return role == "member" and status == "active"
616	
617	
618	def _sweep_delegations(c: sqlite3.Connection, org_id: int, ts: int) -> None:
619	    """Lazy maintenance, called inside write transactions.
620	
621	    * time expiry: active delegations past their expiry become ``expired``
622	      (automatic, no audit row);
623	    * eligibility: an active delegation whose grantor is no longer an active
624	      admin, or whose delegate is no longer an active ordinary member, is
625	      permanently ``invalidated``. The PATCH member endpoints perform the
626	      primary, actor-bearing invalidation; this sweep is the safety net for
627	      state changes that bypass them (e.g. direct on-disk manipulation), and
628	      it records the invalidation with a NULL actor.
629	    """
630	    c.execute(
631	        "UPDATE delegations SET status = 'expired'"
632	        " WHERE org_id = ? AND status = 'active' AND expires_at <= ?",
633	        (org_id, ts),
634	    )
635	    rows = c.execute(
636	        """
637	        SELECT d.id,
638	               gm.role AS g_role, gm.status AS g_status,
639	               dm.role AS d_role, dm.status AS d_status
640	        FROM delegations d
641	        LEFT JOIN memberships gm
642	               ON gm.org_id = d.org_id AND gm.user_id = d.grantor_id
643	        LEFT JOIN memberships dm
644	               ON dm.org_id = d.org_id AND dm.user_id = d.delegate_id
645	        WHERE d.org_id = ? AND d.status = 'active'
646	        """,
647	        (org_id,),
648	    ).fetchall()
649	    for r in rows:
650	        reasons: list[str] = []
651	        if not _grantor_qualifies(r["g_role"], r["g_status"]):
652	            reasons.append("grantor_not_admin")
653	        if not _delegate_qualifies(r["d_role"], r["d_status"]):
654	            reasons.append("delegate_ineligible")
655	        if not reasons:
656	            continue
657	        reason = ",".join(reasons)
658	        c.execute(
659	            "UPDATE delegations SET status = 'invalidated', invalid_reason = ?, invalidated_at = ?"
660	            " WHERE id = ?",
661	            (reason, ts, r["id"]),
662	        )
663	        add_audit(
664	            c, org_id=org_id, actor_id=None, action="delegation.invalidated",
665	            target_type="delegation", target_id=r["id"],
666	            before={"status": "active"},
667	            after={"status": "invalidated", "reason": reason}, ts=ts,
668	        )
669

671	def _invalidate_delegations_for_member_changes(
672	    c: sqlite3.Connection,
673	    *,
674	    org_id: int,
675	    changed_states: dict[int, tuple[str, str]],
676	    actor_id: int,
677	    ts: int,
678	    batch_id: Optional[str] = None,
679	) -> None:
680	    """Permanently invalidate active delegations hit by member role/status edits.
681	
682	    Shared by BOTH PATCH member entry points (single member and batch) so the
683	    eligibility judgement, the delegation status change and the invalidation
684	    audit live in exactly one place; it runs in the SAME transaction as the
685	    membership writes, so the member changes and every invalidation row
686	    commit atomically or roll back together.
687	
688	    ``changed_states`` maps user_id -> (new_role, new_status) for members
689	    that ACTUALLY changed. Only delegations tied to a changed member are
690	    touched: unchanged members get no timestamp update and no audit. Only
691	    ``active`` delegations qualify, so a row already revoked/invalidated is
692	    never recorded twice and its stored reason is never rewritten.
693	    Invalidation is permanent — later restoring role/status never revives
694	    the delegation (only a fresh grant can).
695	
696	    When one delegation's grantor AND delegate both lose eligibility in the
697	    same change set, exactly ONE invalidation row is written; reasons appear
698	    in the fixed grantor-then-delegate order (``grantor_not_admin`` then
699	    ``delegate_ineligible``, comma-joined) and ``triggered_by`` lists the
700	    members actually responsible in that same order without duplicates. The
701	    audit shape follows the entry point: the single-member path (no
702	    ``batch_id``) records ``triggered_by`` as the one member id, while the
703	    batch path records it as a member-id list and stamps ``batch_id``.
704	    """
705	    if not changed_states:
706	        return
707	    affected_ids = list(changed_states.keys())
708	    marks = ",".join("?" for _ in affected_ids)
709	    rows = c.execute(
710	        f"""
711	        SELECT d.id, d.grantor_id, d.delegate_id
712	        FROM delegations d
713	        WHERE d.org_id = ? AND d.status = 'active'
714	          AND (d.grantor_id IN ({marks}) OR d.delegate_id IN ({marks}))
715	        """,
716	        (org_id, *affected_ids, *affected_ids),
717	    ).fetchall()
718	    for r in rows:
719	        reasons: list[str] = []
720	        triggered: list[int] = []
721	        g_state = changed_states.get(r["grantor_id"])
722	        if g_state is not None and not _grantor_qualifies(g_state[0], g_state[1]):
723	            reasons.append("grantor_not_admin")
724	            triggered.append(r["grantor_id"])
725	        d_state = changed_states.get(r["delegate_id"])
726	        if d_state is not None and not _delegate_qualifies(d_state[0], d_state[1]):
727	            reasons.append("delegate_ineligible")
728	            if r["delegate_id"] not in triggered:
729	                triggered.append(r["delegate_id"])
730	        if not reasons:
731	            continue
732	        reason = ",".join(reasons)
733	        c.execute(
734	            "UPDATE delegations SET status = 'invalidated', invalid_reason = ?, invalidated_at = ?"
735	            " WHERE id = ?",
736	            (reason, ts, r["id"]),
737	        )
738	        add_audit(
739	            c, org_id=org_id, actor_id=actor_id, action="delegation.invalidated",
740	            target_type="delegation", target_id=r["id"],
741	            before={"status": "active"},
742	            after={"status": "invalidated", "reason": reason,
743	                   # Single-member path keeps the scalar member id; the batch
744	                   # path carries the ordered, de-duplicated id list.
745	                   "triggered_by": triggered[0] if batch_id is None else triggered},
746	            batch_id=batch_id, ts=ts,
747	        )
748

750	@app.post("/orgs/{org_id}/delegations", status_code=201)
751	def create_delegation(
752	    org_id: int,
753	    body: CreateDelegationRequest,
754	    request_body: bytes = Depends(raw_body),
755	    user: CurrentUser = Depends(current_user),
756	    conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_conn),
757	    idempotency_key: Optional[str] = Header(default=None, alias="Idempotency-Key", max_length=128),
758	) -> dict[str, Any]:
759	    def _perform(c: sqlite3.Connection, ts: int) -> tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]:
760	        # Expired delegations no longer block a fresh grant.
761	        _sweep_delegations(c, org_id, ts)
762	        m = c.execute(
763	            "SELECT * FROM memberships WHERE org_id = ? AND user_id = ?",
764	            (org_id, body.user_id),
765	        ).fetchone()
766	        if m is None or m["role"] != "member" or m["status"] != "active":
767	            # Missing user, non-member, disabled or administrator: one code.
768	            raise conflict("ineligible_member", "target is not an active ordinary member")
769	        existing = c.execute(
770	            "SELECT id FROM delegations"
771	            " WHERE org_id = ? AND delegate_id = ? AND status = 'active'",
772	            (org_id, body.user_id),
773	        ).fetchone()
774	        if existing is not None:
775	            raise conflict("delegation_exists", "member already has an active delegation")
776	        try:
777	            cur = c.execute(
778	                """
779	                INSERT INTO delegations
780	                    (org_id, grantor_id, delegate_id, status,
781	                     created_at, starts_at, expires_at)
782	                VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'active', ?, ?, ?)
783	                """,
784	                (org_id, user.id, body.user_id, ts, ts, ts + body.duration_seconds),
785	            )
786	        except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
787	            # Concurrent grant for the same member: unique partial index.
788	            raise conflict("delegation_exists", "member already has an active delegation")
789	        d_id = cur.lastrowid
790	        add_audit(
791	            c, org_id=org_id, actor_id=user.id, action="delegation.created",
792	            target_type="delegation", target_id=d_id, before=None,
793	            after={"id": d_id, "grantor_id": user.id, "delegate_id": body.user_id,
794	                   "starts_at": ts, "expires_at": ts + body.duration_seconds},
795	            ts=ts,
796	        )
797	        row = c.execute("SELECT * FROM delegations WHERE id = ?", (d_id,)).fetchone()
798	        return 201, delegation_dict(row)
799	
800	    _, resp = _run_idempotent(
801	        conn, user, idempotency.scope_delegation_create(org_id), idempotency_key, request_body,
802	        check_perm=lambda c: require_membership(c, user, org_id, admin=True),
803	        perform=_perform,
804	    )
805	    return resp

897	@app.post("/orgs/{org_id}/invites", status_code=201)
898	def create_invite(
899	    org_id: int,
900	    body: CreateInviteRequest,
901	    request_body: bytes = Depends(raw_body),
902	    user: CurrentUser = Depends(current_user),
903	    conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_conn),
904	    idempotency_key: Optional[str] = Header(default=None, alias="Idempotency-Key", max_length=128),
905	) -> dict[str, Any]:
906	    # Delegation backing the current operation, captured by check_perm and
907	    # consumed by perform inside the SAME transaction (no race possible).
908	    backing: dict[str, Any] = {}
909	
910	    def _check_perm(c: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
911	        m = require_membership(c, user, org_id)
912	        if m["role"] == "admin":
913	            # Administrators need no delegation.
914	            backing["delegation"] = None
915	        else:
916	            # Ordinary members may only issue invites while their delegation
917	            # is active; from the expiry moment on this raises 403.
918	            backing["delegation"] = _active_delegation(c, org_id, user.id, now_ts())
919	
920	    def _replay_check(c: sqlite3.Connection, row: sqlite3.Row) -> None:
921	        # An idempotent retry must still be authorized by the ORIGINAL
922	        # delegation that backed the stored response: if that delegation is
923	        # no longer active the retry is 403, even if a fresh delegation now
924	        # exists. Admin-issued replays require admin membership again.
925	        resp = idempotency.replay_body(row)
926	        d_id = resp.get("delegation_id")
927	        if d_id is None:
928	            require_membership(c, user, org_id, admin=True)
929	            return
930	        d = c.execute(
931	            "SELECT * FROM delegations WHERE id = ? AND org_id = ?", (d_id, org_id)
932	        ).fetchone()
933	        if d is None or d["status"] != "active" or d["expires_at"] <= now_ts():
934	            raise forbidden()
935	
936	    def _perform(c: sqlite3.Connection, ts: int) -> tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]:
937	        d = backing.get("delegation")
938	        delegation_id = d["id"] if d is not None else None
939	        if d is not None and body.role != "member":
940	            # Delegates may only issue member invites.
941	            raise forbidden()
942	        raw_token = generate_invite_token()
943	        expires_at = ts + config.INVITE_TTL_SECONDS
944	        cur = c.execute(
945	            """
946	            INSERT INTO invites
947	                (org_id, token_hash, invite_username, role, status,
948	                 created_by, created_at, expires_at, used_at, used_by, revoked_at,
949	                 delegation_id)
950	            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'available', ?, ?, ?, NULL, NULL, NULL, ?)
951	            """,
952	            (org_id, hash_token(raw_token), body.username, body.role,
953	             user.id, ts, expires_at, delegation_id),
954	        )
955	        invite_id = cur.lastrowid
956	        add_audit(
957	            c, org_id=org_id, actor_id=user.id, action="invite.created",
958	            target_type="invite", target_id=invite_id,
959	            before=None,
960	            after={"id": invite_id, "username": body.username, "role": body.role,
961	                   "status": "available", "expires_at": expires_at,
962	                   "delegation_id": delegation_id},
963	            ts=ts,
964	        )
965	        return 201, {
966	            "id": invite_id,
967	            "org_id": org_id,
968	            "username": body.username,
969	            "role": body.role,
970	            "status": "available",
971	            "token": raw_token,  # returned only here / on idempotent replay
972	            "created_at": ts,
973	            "expires_at": expires_at,
974	            "delegation_id": delegation_id,
975	        }
976	
977	    _, resp = _run_idempotent(
978	        conn, user, idempotency.scope_invite_create(org_id), idempotency_key, request_body,
979	        check_perm=_check_perm, replay_check=_replay_check, perform=_perform,
980	    )
981	    return resp

1033	def accept_invite(
1034	    body: AcceptInviteRequest,
1035	    user: CurrentUser = Depends(current_user),
1036	    conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_conn),
1037	    authorization: Optional[str] = Header(default=None),
1038	    x_session_token: Optional[str] = Header(default=None, alias="X-Session-Token"),
1039	) -> dict[str, Any]:
1040	    # The one session actually carried by THIS request (Bearer or
1041	    # X-Session-Token; ``_extract_token`` keeps the existing precedence).
1042	    # ``current_user`` only proves it was valid when the request arrived;
1043	    # authorization must hold when the join takes effect below.
1044	    request_token = _extract_token(authorization, x_session_token)
1045	    if not request_token:  # defense in depth; current_user already 401s here
1046	        raise unauthorized()
1047	
1048	    # Strict check order per spec:
1049	    # 0) the carried session is still live AT JOIN TIME (re-checked inside
1050	    #    the write transaction)
1051	    # 1) invite availability  2) username match  3) membership state
1052	    with transaction(conn):
1053	        ts = now_ts()
1054	        # Re-validate the EXACT session carried by this request, INSIDE the
1055	        # IMMEDIATE write transaction. BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes this accept
1056	        # against the logout / logout-others / password-change transactions
1057	        # (all writers). Once this check reads the session as live and the
1058	        # transaction goes on to claim the invite, no revocation can be
1059	        # committed in between; and if a revocation committed first — this
1060	        # session logged out, all sessions revoked by a password change, or
1061	        # the expiry instant arrived (expires_at <= now) while the request
1062	        # was waiting — the join fails closed with 401. Another valid login
1063	        # of the same account cannot rescue this session: authorization is
1064	        # keyed to this token hash alone. Nothing is written on this path,
1065	        # so the invite stays available and reusable after a fresh login.
1066	        sess = conn.execute(
1067	            """
1068	            SELECT s.id, s.expires_at, s.revoked_at,
1069	                   u.id AS user_id, u.username AS username
1070	            FROM sessions s JOIN users u ON u.id = s.user_id
1071	            WHERE s.token_hash = ?
1072	            """,
1073	            (hash_token(request_token),),
1074	        ).fetchone()
1075	        if sess is None or sess["revoked_at"] is not None or sess["expires_at"] <= ts:
1076	            raise unauthorized("invalid or expired session")
1077	        actor_id = sess["user_id"]
1078	        actor_username = sess["username"]
1079	
1080	        inv = conn.execute(
1081	            "SELECT * FROM invites WHERE token_hash = ?",
1082	            (hash_token(body.token),),
1083	        ).fetchone()
1084	        if inv is None:
1085	            raise conflict("invite_unavailable", "invite is not available")
1086	        if inv["status"] != "available" or inv["expires_at"] <= ts:
1087	            # expired / revoked / already used all share this code
1088	            raise conflict("invite_unavailable", "invite is not available")
1089	        if inv["invite_username"] != actor_username:
1090	            raise ApiError(403, "username_mismatch", "invite is bound to another user")
1091	        existing = conn.execute(
1092	            "SELECT * FROM memberships WHERE org_id = ? AND user_id = ?",
1093	            (inv["org_id"], actor_id),
1094	        ).fetchone()
1095	        if existing is not None:
1096	            # Existing membership (any role/status) is never overwritten.
1097	            raise conflict("already_member", "user is already a member of the organization")
1098	
1099	        # Conditional claim: only one concurrent acceptor can flip the row.
1100	        cur = conn.execute(
1101	            "UPDATE invites SET status = 'used', used_at = ?, used_by = ?"
1102	            " WHERE id = ? AND status = 'available' AND ? < expires_at",
1103	            (ts, actor_id, inv["id"], ts),
1104	        )
1105	        if cur.rowcount == 0:
1106	            raise conflict("invite_unavailable", "invite is not available")
1107	
1108	        conn.execute(
1109	            "INSERT INTO memberships (org_id, user_id, role, status, created_at, updated_at)"
1110	            " VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'active', ?, ?)",
1111	            (inv["org_id"], actor_id, inv["role"], ts, ts),
1112	        )
1113	        add_audit(
1114	            conn, org_id=inv["org_id"], actor_id=actor_id, action="invite.accepted",
1115	            target_type="membership", target_id=f"{inv['org_id']}:{actor_id}",
1116	            before=None,
1117	            after={"org_id": inv["org_id"], "user_id": actor_id,
1118	                   "role": inv["role"], "status": "active", "invite_id": inv["id"]},
1119	            ts=ts,
1120	        )
1121	        m_row = conn.execute(
1122	            """
1123	            SELECT m.org_id, m.user_id, u.username, m.role, m.status,
1124	                   m.created_at, m.updated_at
1125	            FROM memberships m JOIN users u ON u.id = m.user_id
1126	            WHERE m.org_id = ? AND m.user_id = ?
1127	            """,
1128	            (inv["org_id"], actor_id),
1129	        ).fetchone()
1130	    return {"membership": membership_dict(m_row)}

1135	@app.patch("/orgs/{org_id}/members/batch")
1136	def batch_update_members(
1137	    org_id: int,
1138	    body: BatchUpdateMembersRequest,
1139	    request_body: bytes = Depends(raw_body),
1140	    user: CurrentUser = Depends(current_user),
1141	    conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_conn),
1142	    idempotency_key: Optional[str] = Header(default=None, alias="Idempotency-Key", max_length=128),
1143	) -> dict[str, Any]:
1144	    # Cross-item validation (item shape/enums and the 1..100 bound are already
1145	    # enforced by pydantic -> same stable 422 envelope). These checks run
1146	    # before authorization, matching the single-member entry point.
1147	    seen: set[int] = set()
1148	    for ch in body.changes:
1149	        if ch.role is None and ch.status is None:
1150	            raise ApiError(422, "validation_error", "role or status is required")
1151	        if ch.user_id in seen:
1152	            raise ApiError(422, "validation_error", "duplicate user_id in changes")
1153	        seen.add(ch.user_id)
1154	
1155	    # The one session actually carried by THIS request (Bearer or
1156	    # X-Session-Token; ``current_user`` already applied the existing
1157	    # precedence and proved it valid when the request arrived). That arrival
1158	    # check alone is not enough: the request may then wait behind the write
1159	    # lock, and the session can be logged out, revoked by logout-others or a
1160	    # password change, or reach its expiry while waiting. The batch must be
1161	    # authorized by the session state when it actually takes effect, so the
1162	    # SAME session is re-validated INSIDE the write transaction (see
1163	    # ``_check_perm``) — exactly as the single-member entry point does.
1164	    request_token = user.token
1165	
1166	    def _check_perm(c: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
1167	        # Re-validate the EXACT session this request carries, INSIDE the
1168	        # IMMEDIATE write transaction, before any other check. BEGIN
1169	        # IMMEDIATE serializes this batch against the logout /
1170	        # logout-others / password-change transactions (all writers): once
1171	        # this check reads the session as live and the transaction goes on to
1172	        # change members, no revocation can commit in between; and if a
1173	        # revocation committed first — or the expiry instant arrived
1174	        # (expires_at <= now) while the request was waiting — the whole batch
1175	        # fails closed with 401. Another still-valid session of the same
1176	        # account, or an unchanged administrator identity, cannot rescue this
1177	        # one: authorization is keyed to this token hash alone. Conversely,
1178	        # revoking only the account's OTHER sessions leaves this one live and
1179	        # the batch proceeds.
1180	        #
1181	        # This runs ahead of the membership check (403), the per-target
1182	        # lookups (404), the last-admin invariant (409) and the idempotency
1183	        # lookup (409 / stored replay), so an invalid session is always
1184	        # answered 401 first; and it runs before anything is written, so a
1185	        # 401 here leaves every target's role/status/updated_at untouched,
1186	        # invalidates no delegation and stores no idempotency record — on
1187	        # first attempts (keyed or not) and on replays of a stored success
1188	        # alike (``_run_idempotent`` calls ``check_perm`` on every path
1189	        # before any replay is returned, and a rejected replay never rewrites
1190	        # the stored success).
1191	        revalidate_session(c, request_token, now_ts())
1192	        require_membership(c, user, org_id, admin=True)
1193	
1194	    def _perform(c: sqlite3.Connection, ts: int) -> tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]:
1195	        # Load every target first; a target outside THIS organization fails
1196	        # the whole batch with 404 and reveals nothing about other orgs.
1197	        ordered: list[tuple[sqlite3.Row, str, str]] = []
1198	        for ch in body.changes:
1199	            m = c.execute(
1200	                """
1201	                SELECT m.*, u.username FROM memberships m JOIN users u ON u.id = m.user_id
1202	                WHERE m.org_id = ? AND m.user_id = ?
1203	                """,
1204	                (org_id, ch.user_id),
1205	            ).fetchone()
1206	            if m is None:
1207	                raise not_found("member_not_found", "member not found")
1208	            new_role = ch.role or m["role"]
1209	            new_status = ch.status or m["status"]
1210	            ordered.append((m, new_role, new_status))
1211	
1212	        # Order-independent last-active-admin invariant. Count active admins
1213	        # that are untouched by the batch, then add targeted members whose
1214	        # FINAL state is an active admin (a promotion in the same batch can
1215	        # offset a demotion regardless of list order).
1216	        total_active_admins = c.execute(
1217	            "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM memberships"
1218	            " WHERE org_id = ? AND role = 'admin' AND status = 'active'",
1219	            (org_id,),
1220	        ).fetchone()["n"]
1221	        targeted_active_admins = sum(
1222	            1 for m, _, _ in ordered if m["role"] == "admin" and m["status"] == "active"
1223	        )
1224	        surviving_targeted = sum(
1225	            1 for _, nr, ns in ordered if nr == "admin" and ns == "active"
1226	        )
1227	        untouched_admins = total_active_admins - targeted_active_admins
1228	        if untouched_admins + surviving_targeted == 0:
1229	            raise conflict(
1230	                "last_admin_required",
1231	                "organization must retain at least one active administrator",
1232	            )
1233	
1234	        batch_id = generate_batch_id()
1235	        changed_states: dict[int, tuple[str, str]] = {}
1236	        for m, new_role, new_status in ordered:
1237	            before = {"role": m["role"], "status": m["status"]}
1238	            if new_role != m["role"] or new_status != m["status"]:
1239	                # Unchanged members are returned but keep updated_at and get
1240	                # no audit row.
1241	                c.execute(
1242	                    "UPDATE memberships SET role = ?, status = ?, updated_at = ?"
1243	                    " WHERE id = ?",
1244	                    (new_role, new_status, ts, m["id"]),
1245	                )
1246	                changed_states[m["user_id"]] = (new_role, new_status)
1247	                add_audit(
1248	                    c, org_id=org_id, actor_id=user.id, action="member.updated",
1249	                    target_type="membership", target_id=m["id"],
1250	                    before=before, after={"role": new_role, "status": new_status},
1251	                    batch_id=batch_id, ts=ts,
1252	                )
1253	
1254	        # Delegation invalidation commits in the SAME transaction; one row
1255	        # per affected active delegation even when both parties lose
1256	        # eligibility in this batch.
1257	        _invalidate_delegations_for_member_changes(
1258	            c, org_id=org_id, changed_states=changed_states,
1259	            actor_id=user.id, batch_id=batch_id, ts=ts,
1260	        )
1261	
1262	        # Final member info in SUBMISSION order.
1263	        final_rows: dict[int, sqlite3.Row] = {}
1264	        rows = c.execute(
1265	            """
1266	            SELECT m.org_id, m.user_id, u.username, m.role, m.status,
1267	                   m.created_at, m.updated_at
1268	            FROM memberships m JOIN users u ON u.id = m.user_id
1269	            WHERE m.org_id = ?
1270	            """,
1271	            (org_id,),
1272	        ).fetchall()
1273	        for r in rows:
1274	            final_rows[r["user_id"]] = r
1275	        members_out = [membership_dict(final_rows[ch.user_id]) for ch in body.changes]
1276	        return 200, {"batch_id": batch_id, "members": members_out}
1277	
1278	    _, resp = _run_idempotent(
1279	        conn, user, idempotency.scope_member_batch_update(org_id),
1280	        idempotency_key, request_body,
1281	        check_perm=_check_perm,
1282	        perform=_perform,
1283	    )
1284	    return resp

1670	# Version 1 cursors predate batch filtering and carry no "batch" field; they
1671	# remain valid for unfiltered scans only. Version 2 embeds the filter (the
1672	# exact batch_id, or null for an unfiltered scan) so follow-up requests need

1675	_CURSOR_VERSION_LEGACY = 1

1678	def _encode_scan_cursor(
1679	    org_id: int, end_id: int, position: int, batch_id: Optional[str]
1680	) -> str:
1681	    """Opaque continuation token for an audit scan.
1682	
1683	    The cursor only carries a read position: the organization, the scan's
1684	    fixed upper id bound (the snapshot end), the id of the last entry already
1685	    returned and the batch filter in effect. It is HMAC-signed with the
1686	    server key, so clients can neither read nor alter it, and deterministic,
1687	    so re-issuing a cursor for an unchanged position yields the identical
1688	    string. It never substitutes for authentication — every batch re-checks
1689	    the caller's current admin membership.
1690	    """
1691	    payload = json.dumps(
1692	        {"v": _CURSOR_VERSION, "org": org_id, "end": end_id,
1693	         "pos": position, "batch": batch_id},

1696	    )

1704	    the scan was started with (``None`` for an unfiltered scan). Anything
1705	    unrecognized, tampered with, or minted for another organization raises
1706	    422 invalid_cursor and reveals no audit content. Whether the request is
1707	    ALSO allowed to present its own ``batch_id`` beside the cursor is decided
1708	    by the caller: it must exactly equal the embedded one, and an omitted
1709	    parameter simply adopts it. Legacy (pre-upgrade) cursors embed ``None``,
1710	    so they continue only unfiltered scans.

1712	    try:
1713	        payload = json.loads(verify_signed_text(cursor))
1714	        version = payload["v"]
1715	        end_id = payload["end"]
1716	        position = payload["pos"]
1717	        if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool):
1718	            raise ValueError
1719	        if version == _CURSOR_VERSION_LEGACY:
1720	            cursor_batch: Optional[str] = None
1721	        elif version == _CURSOR_VERSION:
1722	            cursor_batch = payload["batch"]
1723	            if cursor_batch is not None and not isinstance(cursor_batch, str):
1724	                raise ValueError

1730	            or not isinstance(position, int)
1731	            or isinstance(end_id, bool)
1732	            or isinstance(position, bool)
